The four primary cell types in the Drug-seq GDPx2 platform — human aortic smooth muscle cells (AoSMCs), skeletal muscle myoblasts (SkMMs), dermal fibroblasts (DF), and melanocytes (Mel) — show completely distinct baseline transcriptional signatures with no overlap.

Unsupervised k-means clustering (k=4, run on 573 DMSO control samples without using cell-type labels) recovers the known cell types with perfect accuracy: Adjusted Rand Index = 1.0 and Normalized Mutual Information = 1.0. Every sample clusters with its own cell type and none cross over. The first three principal components capture 88.9% of total variance, and the between-cell-type to within-cell-type variance ratio is 34.4-fold, confirming that cell-type identity overwhelmingly dominates the transcriptional structure.

The most similar cell type pair is dermal fibroblasts and skeletal muscle myoblasts, which share the smallest Euclidean centroid distance (102.0 in 20-PC space) and the highest mean pairwise correlation of expression profiles (r = 0.848). Both are mesenchymal/connective tissue derivatives. Melanocytes are the most distinct cell type, showing the largest centroid distances to all others (139–145) and the lowest correlations (r = 0.72–0.75), consistent with their neuroectodermal origin. Aortic smooth muscle cells occupy an intermediate position, clustering closer to the DF–SkMM clade than to melanocytes.

These results validate that the GDPx2 platform produces highly separable baseline transcriptional profiles across the four primary cell types, with clear biological structure that an unsupervised method fully recovers.
